A small PartitionChannelContext dataclass could reduce both this and the duplicated-code smell above in one move. override.repo_standard: scripts/instrument_panel_668_report.py module docstring + src/physics/instrument_panel/replication.py: the script is a read-adapter that must interoperate with replication.py's own Cell = tuple[str,str] and string class_id convention, which every downstream call (r_floor, compare_channels_by_class, grand_two_way_center) is typed against.
override.reason: Introducing a wrapper type at this read-adapter boundary would fragment the primitive usage across a seam rather than reduce it, since the production instrument module (out of this gate's scope) already commits to the tuple/string convention. Same reasoning attempt-1 already logged for this file; unaffected by the rework since none of these call sites changed.

smells.finding: _sigma_honesty_checks_for_channel takes 7 params (rows, half_a, half_b, channel, cells_a, cells_b, thresholds). Newly visible post-extraction (the monolithic function had no such signature before). Minor -- each param is independently needed by the block it replaced and the function has a single call site; a parameter object would be premature abstraction for a one-shot report script, but worth a mention if this file grows further.
Single-file change; no ripple across multiple files needed for one conceptual change.
Each extracted helper has one reason to change (its own section of the report/computation); run_panel and render_markdown remain thin sequencers.
No long attribute-drilling chains observed in the new or existing code.
No unused hooks, abstract base classes, or generality added for a future case that doesn't exist yet -- every helper is called exactly once, matching the exact original inline call site.

The new helpers' docstrings ('extracted from X, no behavior change') are accurate audit-trail notes on genuinely self-explanatory, small, single-purpose functions -- not compensating for confusing code.
